request.system:
You write short rationales for UK property ownership structure options shown to an investment committee.
Rules: each rationale is at most 2 sentences, plain English, and contains NO numbers, digits, percentages or money amounts.
Never state tax amounts or rates. Describe why the structure might suit this packet and investors, and its main trade-off.
Return JSON: {"A": string, "B": string, "C": string, "D": string}.
request.user:
Packet: 5 properties; residential house in england.
Contains residential dwellings: yes.
Investors: Family office (non-UK).
Option A: Buy each property directly. Chain: Family office (non-UK) -> properties.
Option B: One UK SPV owns the portfolio. Chain: Family office (non-UK) -> PropCo Ltd -> properties.
Option C: Fund (unit trust) owns the SPV. Chain: Family office (non-UK) -> JPUT -> PropCo Ltd -> properties.
Option D: Family trust owns the SPV. Chain: Family office (non-UK) (settlor) -> Discretionary trust -> PropCo Ltd -> properties.

response.A: Direct ownership is the simplest route for an overseas family office, with no company or trust to run. The trade-off is that each house is bought and sold separately, non-resident surcharges may apply, and the houses stay exposed to UK inheritance tax in the family's hands.
response.B: One UK SPV holds all the houses as a single package, keeps rental profits inside a company and could make a later sale through a share transfer simpler. The trade-off is that a company owning dwellings can face extra residential charges, and UK rules still look through the shares to the houses for tax on gains and inheritance tax.
response.C: A Jersey unit trust over the SPV is a familiar wrapper for overseas investors, can be tax-transparent for income and makes it easier to bring in co-investors later. The trade-off is offshore set-up and running costs, plus conditions that must be met and kept up for the intended treatment.
response.D: A discretionary trust over the SPV suits an overseas family focused on passing wealth down the generations with flexible control over who benefits. The trade-off is that UK residential property stays within the scope of trust inheritance tax charges, plus extra trust administration and reporting.
